verdict.rationale: Floot documents a chat-driven build loop with checkpoints you can create and restore when a change 'went sideways', plus element pointing and screenshot annotation for targeted follow-up edits. That is a real first-party safety net for iterating. However, the evidence only shows after-the-fact rollback, not that follow-up prompts preserve working features. missing for 10: documentation of scoped or incremental edits that avoid regressions, any diff or review of changes before they apply, and independent or hands-on corroboration of iteration stability.

support.subject: As a founder, I can refine my app through follow-up prompts without breaking what already works

citations.quote: create_checkpoint labels a point you can revert to from the Checkpoint panel in your project view.
Ask it to restore a checkpoint from before the change went sideways.
point at an element or annotate a screenshot for the assistant to pick up
It lets you build and ship full-stack apps without leaving your AI chat
